scientific_question: Do controlled physical interventions on the same camera stream produce transferable observer-response signatures that support held-out causal treatment identification without treating frames as independent replicates?
experimental_unit: one physical block = one day x scene x latent treatment class x replicate; frames within a block are repeated measurements, not independent replicates

event_side.principle: manipulate the local event signal while keeping the nuisance source unchanged

nuisance_side.principle: manipulate background observation nuisance while keeping the local event target unchanged

shared_optical.principle: apply an optical perturbation capable of affecting both local event evidence and scene observability

no_fault.principle: no intentional event-side, nuisance-side or shared optical impairment

phase_summary.paired_response: phase median minus placebo median for each observer channel

diagnostic_intervention_semantics.event_restore: restore or introduce a standard high-visibility local event reference while preserving the current nuisance/optical condition
diagnostic_intervention_semantics.observability_restore: remove or neutralise the nuisance source while preserving the local event target and shared optical condition
diagnostic_intervention_semantics.shared_restore: remove the shared optical impairment while preserving the local event target and nuisance treatment

randomisation.active_phase_order: deterministic SHA256 random permutation within every block

analysis.algorithm: same centroid scaling, first maximin intervention, nearest-two next-intervention rule and nearest-centroid diagnosis as generic V12 API

requirements: dual heldout block accuracy >= best comparator + 0.10
no gross protocol violation in protected QC
A.allowed_claim: Distinct observer responses to controlled physical interventions materially improve held-out causal treatment identification across new days and scenes in the tested physical system.

requirements: dual heldout block accuracy >= best comparator
B.allowed_claim: Physical intervention responses support conditional held-out causal identification, with distinct channels competitive or advantageous under the tested days and scenes.

C.allowed_claim: Physical intervention transfer is mixed across treatments or day-scene blocks; retain boundary results without a general superiority claim.

requirements: dual heldout block accuracy < best comparator - 0.05 OR dual shared-optical recall < 0.50 OR protected QC shows a gross protocol violation that invalidates treatment identity
D.allowed_claim: The preregistered physical intervention protocol does not establish reliable held-out causal treatment identification.

forbidden_claims: treatment compliance is inferred from observer output
physical proxy-event accuracy equals natural pollinator detection accuracy
V13 upgrades V12 beyond its locked B claim
